subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across active memory plugins?
rationale: The code gap is real, but automation cannot safely choose storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, and migration semantics for durable memory lifecycle changes.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Narrow v1 to memory-core
options.body: Implement a bundled memory-core CLI/SQLite lifecycle first, accepting a later compatibility pass for external memory plugins.

options.title: Defer lifecycle MVP
options.body: Leave current search, promotion, Dreaming, and wiki behavior in place and handle concrete stale-memory symptoms separately until lifecycle work is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage and SDK provenance work make this the best available routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
